headline: Middle East tensions spike oil to $93 and the RBA fires its bluntest rate hike warning yet — a tough day for Aussie markets but your long-term holdings remain solid.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 2% last night, likely dragged by broader tech sector caution as investors weigh high AI infrastructure spending against near-term returns. Azure revenue hit a massive $101.9B in FY26, so the fundamentals remain strong — this looks like market noise rather than anything structural.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google edged lower last night alongside the broader tech selloff. News that Berkshire Hathaway holds a stake and Q2 revenue grew 24% year-on-year shows the business is firing — the dip appears to be general market sentiment rather than any company-specific bad news.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 0.74% today in a soft ASX session. Emerging markets ETFs can be sensitive to global risk-off sentiment and a stronger US dollar — the RBA rate hike rhetoric and Middle East tensions likely weighed on broader risk assets today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.52% today, tracking weakness across both the ASX and underlying global equities. Nothing fund-specific here — this is the broader market mood in response to rising interest rate risk and geopolitical uncertainty.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged down 0.26% today, reflecting last night's mild US market dip. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% and NASDAQ was off 0.29% — small moves that shouldn't concern a long-term holder.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO edged up slightly last night. A UK employment tribunal involving Rockstar Games (Take-Two's GTA 6 developer) over alleged unlawful staff sackings is in the news, but the market seems to be treating it as a minor legal matter rather than a business risk.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI held flat today on the ASX. The AI sector remains very much in focus with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra launching today, which is a longer-term positive signal for AI-related holdings, even if today's price didn't move.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS was unchanged today but the background story is more positive than recent price action suggests. Kalkine reports spodumene prices have risen 121% and Pilbara posted record revenue of $1.93B — the lithium cycle may be turning, with battery storage demand driving renewed interest in the sector.

watch_today.title: RBA fires bluntest rate hike warning yet
watch_today.detail: The RBA's Deputy Governor and other senior figures said today that inflation is too high and rates 'may have to rise'. This is the strongest language the RBA has used in this cycle. For you as a long-term investor, a rate hike would pressure growth assets broadly — keep an eye on whether this becomes a hike at the next RBA meeting. It's also a tailwind for PLS.AX and resource stocks if inflation stays sticky.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold — solid fundamentals, last night's dip is noise
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2% last night but Azure revenue hit $101.9B in FY26 — the business is genuinely strong. You're up 12.77% overall on this position. A single rough night in a strong trend is not a reason to do anything. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Hold — GPT-6 Astra launch today is a long-term signal
watch_today.detail: OpenAI just launched GPT-6 Astra, a new flagship AI model. GXAI (Global X AI ETF) is your direct exposure to this sector. You're currently down 13.38% on this position, but the AI investment story — from Pentagon contracts to rapid model releases — remains very much intact. This is a long-term theme. No reason to sell; consider if dips are a buying opportunity for your horizon.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Hold — lithium cycle may be turning
watch_today.detail: PLS was flat today but Kalkine reported spodumene prices up 121% and Pilbara posting record revenue of $1.93B. Battery storage demand is driving a lithium rebound. You're still down 26.85% on this position but the long-term thesis (EV batteries, grid storage) is intact and may be strengthening. Hold and monitor.

watch_today.title: Oil jumps 2.4% on Middle East conflict — watch inflation impact
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) hit $93.69 last night, up 2.42%, as US-Iran tensions flare and Saudi Arabia vows retaliation against Houthi attacks. Higher oil feeds directly into Australian petrol prices and inflation — which is exactly what the RBA is watching. This could be the catalyst that tips the RBA toward a rate hike. Worth watching closely this week.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold — tribunal noise, GTA 6 story intact
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games (owned by Take-Two) is before a UK employment tribunal over alleged unlawful staff dismissals. The market shrugged it off last night — TTWO was up 0.26%. GTA 6 remains one of the most anticipated game launches in history. You're down 7.53% on this position but the long-term thesis is tied to that release. Hold.

world.summary: Middle East conflict escalating with US-Iran fire exchange, oil above $93, and Saudi Arabia threatening retaliation against Houthi attacks. US midterms and Trump-era politics also dominating global headlines.

stories.title: 'Heavy Attack': US and Iran Exchange Fire as Middle East Tensions Escalate
stories.why_it_matters: The US and Iran have directly exchanged fire in what's being described as a 'heavy attack', marking a serious escalation in Middle East tensions. Airlines are only gradually restoring services to the region after halting flights. This is a major geopolitical flashpoint — the last time conflict flared in this region, energy markets moved sharply, and that's exactly what's happening now with oil jumping 2.4% to $93.69 a barrel.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia Vows Retaliation After Houthi Attacks Injure Dozens
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia has pledged to retaliate after Houthi missile and drone attacks injured dozens of people inside the Kingdom. The Houthis, a Yemen-based group backed by Iran, have been targeting Saudi territory and regional shipping. A Saudi counter-attack could widen the conflict significantly and push oil prices even higher — bad news for Australian petrol prices and inflation.

stories.title: Oil Prices Rise on Risk of Protracted Middle East War
stories.why_it_matters: Crude oil (WTI) rose 2.42% to $93.69 last night, directly because of fears the US-Iran and Saudi-Houthi conflicts could drag on for months. For everyday Australians, higher oil means higher petrol prices — and the RBA is already warning about inflation. A prolonged conflict could be the trigger that forces the RBA to raise rates.

stories.title: Trump Locks in Oil Deal with Venezuela — But What About Elections?
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has struck an oil supply deal with Venezuela's Maduro government, raising eyebrows given Maduro's continued hold on power after disputed elections. Venezuelans and democracy advocates are asking why Washington is embracing a government it previously sanctioned. The deal appears motivated by US energy security — getting more oil supply to ease prices — but it signals a pragmatic foreign policy shift that prioritises energy over democracy promotion.

stories.title: Warning Signs for Trump's Republicans as US Midterm Campaign Enters Final Sprint
stories.why_it_matters: Reuters reports multiple warning signs for Trump's Republicans as the US midterm election campaign enters its final stretch. Legal veterans are also organising a fightback against what they call a 'full-out assault on democracy', according to The Guardian. If Democrats regain control of Congress, it could significantly change the US legislative landscape — affecting everything from trade policy to regulation of US tech companies that you hold (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO).

markets.summary: The ASX 200 fell 1% today — a solid drop — as the RBA's rate hike threat and surging oil prices unnerved investors. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 and NASDAQ were both mildly negative. Oil is the big mover, up 2.4% to $93.69 on Middle East tensions. Gold hit $4,447 — investors are clearly seeking safety. The Aussie dollar held steady at about 72 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Dropped 1% today — the RBA's blunt rate hike warning and surging oil prices hit confidence across the board.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Mild loss last night — tech stocks led the drag as investors stayed cautious heading into a busy geopolitical week.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slightly lower last night, with Microsoft and Google both falling. The AI spending story is strong but the market is in a 'show me' mood.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big jump last night on US-Iran tensions and Saudi Arabia's retaliation threat. Higher oil means higher petrol and more inflation pressure.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold ticked higher as investors sought safety amid Middle East conflict and rate uncertainty. At $4,447 it remains historically elevated.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was steady, up slightly. A potential RBA rate hike could provide further support to AUD in coming weeks.

politics.summary: The RBA fired its strongest rate hike warning yet today, with multiple senior figures saying inflation is too high and rates 'may have to rise'. Meanwhile, the federal government is pushing new social media algorithm laws and workers could be in line for a pay boost.

stories.title: RBA's Bluntest Warning Yet: Inflation Too High, Rate Hike May Be Coming
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said today that 'people are furious' about inflation and that the RBA 'may have to raise' the cash rate if inflation doesn't come down fast enough. This is the most direct language the RBA has used in this cycle. For mortgage holders and anyone with debt, this is a serious heads-up that another rate hike is on the table. For investors, rising rates typically put pressure on growth assets and can weigh on the ASX. Spiking oil prices are adding fuel to the inflation fire.

stories.title: New Laws to Force Social Media Giants to Offer Algorithm Opt-Out
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is pushing new legislation that would require social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to give Australians the option to opt out of algorithm-driven feeds — meaning you could choose a chronological feed instead of one curated to maximise engagement. Labor has not ruled out that platforms could pull out of Australia entirely rather than comply, similar to what happened with news content. This follows Australia's earlier moves on social media age limits.

stories.title: One Nation's Early Super Access Plan Rejected by Federal Government
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government has come out against One Nation's proposal to let Australians access their superannuation early. The government argues early access undermines the purpose of super — long-term retirement savings — and could leave people worse off in retirement. For investors, it's a signal that the super system's integrity (and the massive pool of capital it represents) is being defended, which is broadly positive for long-term market stability.

stories.title: Millions of Workers Tipped for $2,500 Pay Boost Under Job-Hopping Overhaul
stories.why_it_matters: A proposed overhaul of job mobility rules could see millions of Australian workers receive a $2,500 pay boost by making it easier to switch jobs and take their entitlements with them. The idea is to reward workers who change roles rather than penalise them under outdated employment rules. For consumers, more money in pockets is a spending boost — though the RBA would note it could also add to wage-driven inflation pressure at exactly the wrong time.

ai.summary: OpenAI dropped GPT-6 Astra today — a significant new flagship model — while robots literally marched in Poland demanding stronger AI regulation, and US defence contracts with AI giants are drawing fresh scrutiny.

stories.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Astra — A New Generation of Intelligence
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI today released GPT-6 Astra, its newest flagship AI model, marking another major step forward in the rapid AI model race. This comes as competitors Claude Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash are also on the market, with reports of a 13x price gap between the top models. For your GXAI.AX holding (Global X AI ETF), this ongoing AI arms race is exactly the kind of activity that drives the sector's long-term growth story.

stories.title: 30 Robots March in Poland Demanding Stronger AI Rules and Warning of Job Losses
stories.why_it_matters: A Polish tech company organised a street protest with 30 actual robots marching through the city, holding signs demanding tighter AI regulation and warning that unchecked AI could cost millions of jobs. It's a clever publicity stunt but it reflects a real and growing debate: as AI gets more capable, who is responsible for the harm it causes? The protest is generating global attention and adding pressure on governments — including Australia — to act faster on AI rules.

stories.title: AI Giants Working Hand-in-Hand With the Pentagon, Contracts Reveal
stories.why_it_matters: Newly revealed US Defence Department contracts show major AI companies — including firms like Google and Microsoft — are deeply embedded in Pentagon operations, from logistics to intelligence tools. This raises ethical questions about AI being used in military decision-making, but for investors it also confirms that AI revenue is being underpinned by massive government contracts, adding stability to the business models of companies like Google (your GOOG holding).

stories.title: The House Democrat Making AI Regulation Her Top Priority
stories.why_it_matters: A US House Democrat is pushing AI regulation as her top legislative priority, working on bipartisan bills to set guardrails around AI use in hiring, healthcare, and national security. With AI companies raking in Pentagon contracts and releasing powerful new models weekly, regulatory momentum in the US is building. New rules could affect how quickly companies like Google and Microsoft can deploy AI products — something to watch for your tech holdings.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 1 is locked in with team lists confirmed. Kayo Sports smashed streaming records in Round 27. AFL trade and injury news is swirling as the season hits its business end.

stories.title: NRL 2026 Finals Week 1: Every Club's Confirmed Lineup
stories.why_it_matters: All four Finals Week 1 team lists are now confirmed. Key matchups include Rabbitohs vs Knights (Friday night at Allianz Stadium), Warriors vs Dolphins (Saturday at Go Media Stadium), Sharks vs Cowboys (Saturday night at Allianz), and the blockbuster Panthers vs Roosters (Sunday at CommBank Stadium). Check the NRL draw in the app for full kick-off times.

stories.title: Kayo Sports Shatters NRL Streaming Records — Most-Watched Game Ever Revealed
stories.why_it_matters: Kayo Sports broke all-time NRL streaming records in Round 27, with the most-watched game in the platform's history recorded. The NRL's streaming audience is surging heading into finals, which bodes well for the competition's TV rights value and the overall health of the game.

stories.title: AFL: Brisbane Star Speaks on Future After Contract Bombshell
stories.why_it_matters: A Brisbane Lions star has publicly addressed his future after a major contract decision, with the AFL trade period looming. Separately, AFL injury news today includes a Cats midfielder who may miss the rest of the season, and a Lion needing to prove fitness. With finals underway and the trade period approaching, contract and injury news will be driving headlines daily.

stories.title: NRL Signings Tracker: Seve Calls Time on Career; Young Locked In Long-Term
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL signings tracker is heating up with finals underway. Veteran Seve has confirmed he's retiring, while another player (Young) has signed a long-term extension. The Bulldogs are also reportedly set to sign the younger brother of an exiled NRL star, and the Raiders CEO says he's 'quietly confident' of re-signing a key player. The off-season player market is already moving.
